name: Riblah
overview: Riblah is identified in Scripture as a significant border town marking the eastern limits of the Promised Land (Numbers 34:11). It also served as a place of captivity and judgment, where Pharaoh Nechoh detained King Jehoahaz to prevent his reign over Jerusalem, imposing tribute on the land (2 Kings 23:33). Furthermore, Riblah was the military headquarters of King Nebuchadnezzar during the siege and eventual fall of Jerusalem, where he executed judgment on the captured king and his people, leading to the exile of Judah (2 Kings 25:6, 20-21). These accounts highlight Riblah's strategic and judicial importance in the unfolding history of God's people.
